{{Short description|Statistical relationship in stochastic processes}}
In probability, '''weak dependence of random variables''' is a generalization of [[Independent random variables|independence]] that is weaker than the concept of a [[Martingale (probability)|martingale]]{{citation needed|date=May 2020}}.  A (time) [[sequence]] of [[random variable]]s is weakly dependent if distinct portions of the sequence have a [[covariance]] that [[asymptotically]] decreases to 0 as the blocks are further separated in time.  Weak dependence primarily appears as a technical condition in various [[Central limit theorem|probabilistic limit theorems]].

== Formal definition ==
Fix a set {{mvar|S}}, a sequence of sets of [[measurable function]]s <math>\{\mathcal{F}_d\}_{d=1}^{\infty}\in\prod_{d=1}^{\infty}{\left(S^d\to\mathbb{R}\right)}</math>, a decreasing sequence <math>\{\theta_{\delta}\}_{\delta=1}^{\infty}\to0</math>, and a function <math>\psi\in\mathcal{F}^2\times(\mathbb{Z}^+)^2\to\mathbb{R}^+</math>.  A sequence <math>\{X_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}</math> of random variables is <math>(\{\mathcal{F}_d\}_{d=1}^{\infty},\{\theta_{\delta}\}_{\delta},\psi)</math>-weakly dependent iff, for all <math>j_1\leq j_2\leq\dots\leq j_d<j_d+\delta\leq k_1\leq k_2\leq\dots\leq k_e</math>, for all <math>\phi\in\mathcal{F}_d</math>, and <math>\theta\in\mathcal{F}_e</math>, we have<ref name="Doukhan 1999">{{Cite journal|date=1999-12-01|title=A new weak dependence condition and applications to moment inequalities|journal=Stochastic Processes and Their Applications|language=en|volume=84|issue=2|pages=313–342|doi=10.1016/S0304-4149(99)00055-1|issn=0304-4149|last1=Doukhan|first1=Paul|last2=Louhichi|first2=Sana|doi-access=free}}</ref>{{Rp|315}}

: <math>|\operatorname{Cov}{(\phi(X_{j_1},\dots,X_{j_d}), \theta(X_{k_1},\dots,X_{k_e}))}|\leq\psi(\phi,\theta,d,e)\theta_{\delta}</math>

Note that the covariance does ''not'' decay to {{Math|0}} uniformly in {{mvar|d}} and {{mvar|e}}.<ref name="Dedecker 2007">{{Cite book|date=2007 |volume=190|language=en-gb|doi=10.1007/978-0-387-69952-3|isbn=978-0-387-69951-6|last1=Dedecker|first1=Jérôme|last2=Doukhan|first2=Paul|last3=Lang|first3=Gabriel|last4=Louhichi|first4=Sana|last5=Leon|first5=José Rafael|last6=José Rafael|first6=León R.|last7=Prieur|first7=Clémentine|title=Weak Dependence: With Examples and Applications |series=Lecture Notes in Statistics }}</ref>{{Rp|9}}  

== Common applications ==
Weak dependence is a sufficient weak condition that many natural instances of stochastic processes exhibit it.<ref name="Dedecker 2007" />{{Rp|9}}  In particular, weak dependence is a natural condition for the ergodic theory of random functions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wu|first1=Wei Biao|authorlink1=Wei Biao Wu|last2=Shao|first2=Xiaofeng|date=June 2004|title=Limit theorems for iterated random functions|journal=Journal of Applied Probability|language=en|volume=41|issue=2|pages=425–436|doi=10.1239/jap/1082999076|s2cid=335616|issn=0021-9002}}</ref>

A sufficient substitute for independence in the [[Lindeberg–Lévy central limit theorem]] is weak dependence.<ref name="Doukhan 1999" />{{Rp|315}}  For this reason, specializations often appear in the probability literature on limit theorems.<ref name="Dedecker 2007" />{{Rp|153–197}}  These include Withers' condition for strong mixing,<ref name="Doukhan 1999" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Withers|first=C. S.|date=December 1981|title=Conditions for linear processes to be strong-mixing|journal=Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und Verwandte Gebiete|language=en|volume=57|issue=4|pages=477–480|doi=10.1007/bf01025869|s2cid=122082639|issn=0044-3719|doi-access=free}}</ref> Tran's "absolute regularity in the locally transitive sense,"<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tran|first=Lanh Tat|title=Recursive kernel density estimators under a weak dependence condition|journal=Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics|language=en|volume=42|issue=2|pages=305–329|doi=10.1007/bf00050839|issn=0020-3157|year=1990|s2cid=120632192}}</ref> and Birkel's  "asymptotic quadrant independence."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1992-07-11|title=Laws of large numbers under dependence assumptions|journal=Statistics & Probability Letters|language=en|volume=14|issue=5|pages=355–362|doi=10.1016/0167-7152(92)90096-N|issn=0167-7152|last1=Birkel|first1=Thomas}}</ref>

Weak dependence also functions as a substitute for [[strong mixing]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wu|first=Wei Biao|authorlink=Wei Biao Wu|date=2005-10-04|title=Nonlinear system theory: Another look at dependence|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=102|issue=40|pages=14150–14154|doi=10.1073/pnas.0506715102|issn=0027-8424|pmid=16179388|pmc=1242319|bibcode=2005PNAS..10214150W|doi-access=free}}</ref>  Again, generalizations of the latter are specializations of the former; an example is [[M. Rosenblatt|Rosenblatt]]'s mixing condition.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rosenblatt|first=M.|date=1956-01-01|title=A Central Limit Theorem and a Strong Mixing Condition|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=42|issue=1|pages=43–47|doi=10.1073/pnas.42.1.43|issn=0027-8424|pmid=16589813|pmc=534230|bibcode=1956PNAS...42...43R|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Other uses include a generalization of the [[Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund inequality]] and [[Rosenthal inequalities]].<ref name="Doukhan 1999" />{{Rp|314,319}}

[[Martingale (probability)|Martingales]] are weakly dependent {{citation needed|date=May 2020}}, so many results about martingales also hold true for weakly dependent sequences.  An example is [[Bernstein inequalities (probability theory)|Bernstein's bound on higher moments]], which can be relaxed to only require<ref name="fan">{{cite journal|last1=Fan|first1=X.|last2=Grama|first2=I.|last3=Liu|first3=Q.|year=2015|title=Exponential inequalities for martingales with applications|journal=Electronic Journal of Probability|volume=20|pages=1–22|doi=10.1214/EJP.v20-3496|arxiv=1311.6273|s2cid=119713171}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bernstein|first=Serge|date=December 1927|title=Sur l'extension du théorème limite du calcul des probabilités aux sommes de quantités dépendantes|journal=Mathematische Annalen|language=fr|volume=97|issue=1|pages=1–59|doi=10.1007/bf01447859|s2cid=122172457|issn=0025-5831}}</ref>

: <math>\begin{align}
\operatorname{E} \left [ X_i \mid X_1, \dots, X_{i-1} \right ] &= 0, \\
\operatorname{E} \left [ X_i^2 \mid X_1, \dots, X_{i-1} \right ] &\leq R_i \operatorname{E} \left [ X_i^2 \right ], \\
\operatorname{E} \left [ X_i^k \mid X_1, \dots, X_{i-1} \right ] &\leq  \tfrac{1}{2} \operatorname{E} \left[ X_i^2 \mid X_1, \dots, X_{i-1} \right ] L^{k-2} k!
\end{align}</math>
